semanticAssessment: The target executed (1 test, 1 failure, 0 errors) and failed on the planned publish assertion with its own EAGER_TASK_HINT message. The RED came from the same named temporary mutant as Task 1 in custom_components/mqtt_actions/takeover.py: in _remove_planned, the disable-first step of an enabled row was replaced by pass, so the replay catch removes the two loaded test buttons while their entities are still subscribed. Core MQTT then publishes its clear-on-remove for each (two retained None payloads on the shared topic). That is the same observable effect as a Home Assistant core without the eager task in Entity._async_registry_updated, where the disable would not unsubscribe the entity before the remove event. The premise held under the mutant: the catch call carried LEGACY content and saw the switch disabled and both buttons loaded and enabled; the buttons left the registry and the integration-disabled switch twin stayed (09.2 D-05), so only the publish assertion caught the change, which is the intended reason. No import, collection or fixture fault. The mutant was reverted with git checkout before the commit and git diff --quiet -- custom_components/ was clean.
